requirements.text: Reception-security post from 9:00 to 19:00, Tuesday to Saturday; one SSIAP 1 fire-safety officer present for all public opening hours.
Night patrols every 2 h from 20:00 to 6:00, checked with tags and recorded in an electronic log.
Every officer holds a valid CNAPS professional licence; copy supplied before taking up the post.
The company and its directors hold the CNAPS operating authorisation.
Fire-safety officers qualified SSIAP 1, team leader SSIAP 2, refresher training up to date.
Alarm response with on-site verification in under 30 minutes, 24/7.
Written report to the buyer within 24 h of any incident.
Staff transfer under the security-sector collective agreement (IDCC 1351); 5 officers concerned, list in appendix 4.
Any absent officer is replaced within 2 h; no shift left uncovered.
Each officer is trained on the site orders before taking up the post (minimum 4 h shadowing).
Remote monitoring may be subcontracted after declaration (DC4) and buyer approval.
Hourly BPU per grade (guard, SSIAP 1, SSIAP 2) with night, Sunday and public-holiday uplifts; annual DQE simulation completed without changing quantities.
Identifiable uniform marked “Sécurité”; professional licence visible at all times.

chunks.title: Past proposal — Brume-sur-Lys museum, reception-security and SSIAP (2024)
chunks.text: For Brume-sur-Lys museum (fictional): reception-security post during opening hours, one SSIAP 1 officer permanently at the fire-safety desk, bag checks at peak times, electronic log shared with the venue team.

chunks.title: Procedure — Night patrols and electronic log
chunks.text: Patrols every 2 h on varied routes, NFC tags at each sensitive point. Any anomaly entered in the electronic log with photo and time; the client has read access.

chunks.title: Register — Officers' CNAPS professional licences
chunks.text: Register of 42 (fictional) officers with licence number, expiry date and automatic alert 90 days before expiry. Copy given to the client before each new posting.

chunks.title: CNAPS operating authorisation — company and directors
chunks.text: Company operating authorisation and directors' approvals (fictional numbers for the demo), valid, attached to every application.

chunks.title: Training plan — SSIAP 1 and 2, refreshers
chunks.text: SSIAP refresher schedule over 3 years, skills maintenance run in-house. SSIAP 2 team leaders on every site with more than 300 visitors.

chunks.title: CV — Karim Benali, SSIAP 2 site manager
chunks.text: Karim Benali (fictional person): 10 years in public-venue security, SSIAP 2 site manager for 6 years, leads up to 12 officers, runs evacuation drills.

chunks.title: Flowchart — Alarm response and on-site verification
chunks.text: Alarm received → call to site → mobile patrol dispatched → on-site verification → site secured → written report to the client within 24 h. Average arrival time in 2025: 18 minutes (fictional internal figure).

chunks.title: Procedure — Staff transfer (security-sector agreement)
chunks.text: Steps: receive the outgoing contractor's list, brief the officers, one-to-one interview, licence check, contract amendment, seniority kept. Timeline aligned on the start date.

chunks.title: Continuity plan — cover within 2 h
chunks.text: Pool of 8 officers trained on several sites' orders, 24/7 supervisory on-call. Internal target: replacement on post within 2 h.

chunks.title: Sheet — Site-order induction (shadowing)
chunks.text: Each new officer shadows a regular officer for at least 4 h, then answers a quiz on general and specific orders, signed off by the site manager.

chunks.title: Framework contract — Remote monitoring (declared subcontractor)
chunks.text: Remote monitoring by a usual (fictional) subcontractor, declared on a DC4 for each contract and subject to buyer approval. Alarm hand-off protocol to our mobile patrol.

bullets.text: Reception-security post from 9:00 to 19:00, Tuesday to Saturday, on the model already running at Brume-sur-Lys museum.
Night patrols every 2 h from 20:00 to 6:00, NFC tags and an electronic log the buyer can read.
CNAPS licences tracked in a register with an alert 90 days before expiry; copies supplied before each posting.
Company operating authorisation and directors' approvals attached.
SSIAP 1 officers, SSIAP 2 team leader, refreshers scheduled.
At least 4 h shadowing on the site orders before any posting.
Alarm response by mobile patrol, following our verification flowchart.
Written report to the buyer within 24 h of any incident.
Remote monitoring by our usual subcontractor, declared on a DC4 and subject to buyer approval.
Transfer of the 5 officers in appendix 4 under the sector agreement: briefing, interview, licence check, amendment, seniority kept.
Cover within 2 h thanks to a pool of 8 officers and 24/7 supervisory on-call.
Hourly BPU completed per grade, with night, Sunday and public-holiday uplifts; DQE completed without changing quantities.
